title: Republicans Embrace the Vice Economy | Institute for Family Studies
gist: An IFS-syndicated excerpt of a Compact Magazine piece argues Republicans, despite their 'family values' self-image, have repeatedly sided with the 'vice economy' — delaying a ban on intoxicating hemp-derived products, rescheduling marijuana by executive order, and curtailing regulatory scrutiny of cryptocurrency and prediction markets — as marijuana use overtakes alcohol and tobacco.

insights.claim: Marijuana use has surpassed alcohol and tobacco use for the first time, according to the article, coinciding with a string of pro-vice-economy policy wins delivered by Republicans.
insights.speaker: Brad Wilcox, James Lynch
insights.so_what: A notable consumption-trend data point for the cannabis and legacy alcohol/tobacco industries, framed as a backdrop to Republican-driven deregulation of vice products.
insights.quote: As marijuana use surpasses alcohol and tobacco use for the first time, Republicans have delivered another win for the vice economy.

insights.claim: Figures including Donald Trump and Rand Paul successfully pushed to delay a ban on intoxicating hemp-derived products, which the article frames as the latest in a series of pro-vice moves by the GOP.
insights.speaker: Brad Wilcox, James Lynch
insights.so_what: Signals continued regulatory tailwinds for the intoxicating-hemp product category rather than an incoming ban, relevant for cannabis/hemp-adjacent consumer-goods investors.
insights.quote: Figures ranging from Donald Trump to Rand Paul successfully pushed to delay a ban on intoxicating hemp-derived products.

insights.claim: The article lists Republican rescheduling of marijuana by executive order and reduced regulatory scrutiny of cryptocurrency and prediction markets as part of the same pro-vice-economy policy pattern alongside the hemp delay.
insights.speaker: Brad Wilcox, James Lynch
insights.so_what: Groups marijuana rescheduling with lighter-touch crypto and prediction-market oversight as part of one coherent deregulatory trend under GOP leadership, a relevant signal for regulatory-risk assessment in both sectors.
insights.quote: This is the latest in a string of pro-vice moves from the GOP, ranging from rescheduling marijuana by executive order to curtailing regulatory scrutiny on cryptocurrency and prediction markets.

insights.claim: The authors argue this pro-vice policy record is at odds with the Republican Party's self-conception as champions of American virtues such as thrift, hard work, and sobriety, calling out the party of 'family values' for becoming partisans of Big Weed and online gambling.
insights.speaker: Brad Wilcox, James Lynch
insights.so_what: Frames a values-based critique that could shape intra-GOP debate over vice-industry deregulation, relevant to political-risk tracking for cannabis, gambling, and crypto sectors reliant on continued light-touch regulation.
insights.quote: But too many in the party of “family values” have become partisans for the vice economy.
